<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/platform-system-api.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 03bce5c22a473cca2ca03eb85d0ca489783d610d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1bc97c873d5a93302843661ec408d7f651fc335c` — the merge of head `0a28c2810934861aaadc66e469e2af4295c216dd` into base `03bce5c22a473cca2ca03eb85d0ca489783d610d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1bc97c873d5a93302843661ec408d7f651fc335c && git checkout 1bc97c873d5a93302843661ec408d7f651fc335c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 03bce5c22a473cca2ca03eb85d0ca489783d610d 0a28c2810934861aaadc66e469e2af4295c216dd && git checkout -B drift-repro 03bce5c22a473cca2ca03eb85d0ca489783d610d && git merge --no-ff 0a28c2810934861aaadc66e469e2af4295c216dd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 03bce5c22a473cca2ca03eb85d0ca489783d610d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 03bce5c22a473cca2ca03eb85d0ca489783d610d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1: ACCEPT** (L1-a, for area d7-B) at head `186bbc489c00f71d513eac6e3550aa13fa820ffb`, read 2026-11-20T04:41Z. One PR-body correction is owed; it moves no head (see the end).

Checklist (`l1-review-checklist.md`), read on GitHub and in the head tree:

- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, `Fixes #35434`, the card delivered whole. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` sit at line start in the body and the new changeset.
- **Route B is sound.**
  - `DISPATCHED_ACTION_APIS` is a module-local `WeakSet<ScopedContext>`. Only `ObjectRepositoryFacet.execute` sets it on a fresh api, and only `ScopedContextFacet.derive` copies it, on the instance's own `facade`.
  - `markDispatchedActionApi` / `isDispatchedActionApi` are module exports only. No package entry re-exports `engine-object-repository` or `engine-scoped-context` (checked with a grep of the head), so there is no new public name, and `Clause-②: no` stands.
  - `engine.ts` is untouched, so the `check:facade-delegation-only` ceiling is unaffected. The new import from `engine-scoped-context` into `engine-object-repository` is read only at call time, never at module evaluation, so the import cycle through `engine.js` is inert.
  - The flag can only tighten. On a flagged api, `platformSystemApi` answers the api's own `sudo()`: mark and `flowRunId` kept, so more writes are judged as an action body's, never fewer.
  - The flag is not the app-authored flag, so ADR-0148 D3's permanent-delete refusal does not newly bite a dispatched host handler.
  - `buildHookApi` still builds a fresh, unflagged `ScopedContext`, so the audit writer's platform write is unchanged.
  - Route A being measured infeasible (it would change `ObjectRepository`'s published constructor, and objectql never sees runtime's wrapper) is a fair basis for B. B and A give the same behaviour; C would differ, so choosing B decided no product question.
- **Boundary.** This changes a permission outcome, so I checked that it decides no new boundary. It enforces one already documented: row 1b says an action body's writes to the four identity-assignment objects are refused, and the `execute` path was the documented carve-out (L2 7003367719 S2, filed as a Bug). Removing a gap in a ruled refusal is not a human-floor decision.
- **Point (1): refusal pinned with code and status, and two ablations.** Met.
  - The shared assertion helper checks `err.code` `PERMISSION_DENIED` and `statusCode ?? status` `403`, plus "nothing lands", across all four identity-assignment objects, three routes (direct, `sudo()`, transaction) and two dispatchers (the action door's api and a bare engine api). It runs on a real `ObjectQL`, the SQL driver and the real `SecurityPlugin`.
  - Controls: the owner stamp, the code-registered hook's platform write landing, and the dispatched handler's permanent delete.
  - Base reading 9/11 red. Ablation 1 (`execute` stops flagging): 9 red. Ablation 2 (`derive` stops copying): 8 red, only the `sudo()` / transaction routes plus the owner stamp, the direct route green, exactly the shape the copy predicts. Both were rebuilt into dist with the preflight marker and restored blob-equal.
- **Prose, sentence by sentence.**
  - New changeset: each bullet matches the code and a pin. The last sentence, "No new export, and no published signature changes", is true per the grep above.
  - `system-context.mdx` row 1b and the `platform-system-api.ts` header: only the "Not covered … still takes the mark off" sentence is removed. Row 2's "and by `ObjectRepository.execute`" (the mark) remains true.
- **DELIBERATE CORRECTION.** The two `Check Changeset` reds are both `check-empty-changeset`'s foreign-note refusal on exactly one file, `.changeset/35174-action-api-platform-system-api-mark.md`. I read the job log, and it names only that note. That note is pending, from PR #35383. Before: "- Not covered: the api `ctx.api.object(o).execute(name)` hands the action it dispatches is built by the engine, not the action door, so `platformSystemApi` still takes the mark off there." After: the bullet is removed, and no other sentence of that note changes. The removed sentence is false at this head (ablation 1 is exactly that path), so removing it is right, and restoring it would republish a false sentence. This diff changes code, so under `landing-operations.md` the confirmation that counts is a same-head at-tier L2 PASS that judges this rewrite; this L1 ACCEPT alone does not confirm it.
- **Gates.** CI at `186bbc48`: 40 `success`, 17 `skipped`, and 2 `failure`, both the `Check Changeset` refusal above. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Test Core` are `success`.
- **Scope.** `engine-scoped-context.ts` went beyond the claim's "only if route A" wording, and the body declares it with the reason (B needs `derive` and the facet body). Overlap is clean, and #35541 has merged. Accepted. The 35174 note edit sits outside the claim surface as a seat amendment, declared above.

**Point (2): L2.** None of the four contract faces is touched (no `Clause-②: yes`, no narrowing arm, no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path). The same-head `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` L2 is owed anyway, because the DELIBERATE CORRECTION on a code diff is confirmed only by that record, and it must judge the rewritten sentence of the 35174 note. Running it after this ACCEPT is fine; I see no reason to run it first. Brief the isolated reviewer with the diff and the two notes, not with this verdict.

**Owed before the L2 and before landing: a PR-body correction.** `## Acceptance notes` still says the pending changeset `.changeset/35174-action-api-platform-system-api-mark.md` "is outside this card's file surface and is not edited here". The diff edits it, and the body's own `## DELIBERATE CORRECTION` section says so. Rewrite that bullet to match, for example "edited here as a seat amendment; see DELIBERATE CORRECTION". It is a body edit and moves no head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `186bbc489c00f71d513eac6e3550aa13fa820ffb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/35174-action-api-platform-system-api-mark.md, .changeset/35434-execute-dispatched-action-keeps-mark.md + packages/objectql/src/engine-object-repository.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-scoped-context.ts, packages/objectql/src/platform-system-api.ts, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx
Security-touching: yes

Read: card #35434 (body and all 5 comments), the PR body and its 7-file list, the net diff against merge base `97f342037d`, the check-runs on the head, and the log of Check Changeset job 136077577385. `packages/runtime/src/execute-dispatched-action-platform-system-api-35434.integration.test.ts` was read as evidence. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface: none added. Right.** `markDispatchedActionApi` and `isDispatchedActionApi` are `export`ed from the module `engine-object-repository.ts` only. `packages/objectql/package.json` `exports` has two entries, `.` and `./core`; `src/index.ts` and `src/core.ts` re-export `ObjectQL`, `ObjectRepository`, `ScopedContext` from `./engine.js` and `platformSystemApi` from `./platform-system-api.js` by name, and neither names `engine-object-repository` or `engine-scoped-context`. The only importer of the two helpers is `engine-scoped-context.ts:56`. Not reachable from a package entry.
- **Published class faces: unchanged. Right.** `ScopedContext` gains no member (the flag is a module `WeakSet`, `derive` stays private at `engine.ts:6469`); `ObjectRepository`'s constructor and `execute` signature are untouched; `engine.ts` is not in the diff. The two facet `this` types widen by `'facade'`, an existing `ScopedContextHost` key (`engine.ts:6846`, `facade: instance`); the facet is not exported from either entry.
- **Accept-set change: one narrowing of a permission outcome, at the consumer the card names. Right.** On the api `ObjectRepositoryFacet.execute` builds, and on every api `derive` builds from it, `ScopedContext#[PLATFORM_SYSTEM_API]` now answers `sudo()` (mark and `flowRunId` kept) where it stripped both. So an insert, update or delete of `sys_member`, `sys_user_position`, `sys_user_permission_set`, `sys_invitation` through it is refused by plugin-security, and an insert into an ordinary object is owner-stamped. Nothing else changes outcome: the dispatched handler's direct writes and its `sudo()` already carried the mark at the merge base (the test's `ownSudo` control).
- **Dual build: right.** The `WeakSet` is module-local, so each built copy holds its own. The writer (`execute`, reached through an `ObjectRepository` of copy X) constructs copy X's `ScopedContext`, and both readers are reached through that instance's own stubs (`derive`, `[PLATFORM_SYSTEM_API]`), which call copy X's facet. Writer and reader cannot be different copies. The header's sentence saying so holds.
- **Gate verdicts, from the head's check-runs.** Every concluded run is `success` or `skipped` except Check Changeset (red twice, a third run in progress at read time). In job 136077577385 the one failed step is `Reject an empty-frontmatter changeset added by this PR`, and its one error is the M row on `.changeset/35174-action-api-platform-system-api-mark.md` (the COLLISION / DELIBERATE CORRECTION refusal). Its other steps passed: a changeset is present, 2 declaring changesets, no `major`, LEVEL AXIS `patch` with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. The red is the declared class and nothing else.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/35434-execute-dispatched-action-keeps-mark.md`: `@objectstack/objectql` `patch`. Right. The published change is in objectql's `src` alone; the runtime file is a test, the docs page ships in no package. A bug fix with no surface change is a patch.
- `.changeset/35174-action-api-platform-system-api-mark.md`: frontmatter unchanged (`@objectstack/runtime` `patch`); the diff is one deleted line.
- Clause-②: no. Agreed: no export added, removed or re-typed at either entry, no `packages/spec/src` path, no governed path, no schema. No `(narrowing)` arm is declared and none is owed by face: the tightened outcome is a refusal the page already states for an action body, on an api the same page said was missed (see ④).
- Metadata-protocol: none. Agreed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation: `engine-scoped-context.ts` touched under route B.** Accepted. `derive` and the `platformSystemApi` facet body are in that file, and route B cannot keep the flag across `sudo()` or a transaction without `derive` (the PR's second ablation is that case). #35541 is merged into the branch; Type Check and Test Core are green on the head.
- **Deviation: PR body section order.** No contract effect. PR-body guards are green.
- **Deviation: two overlapping local gate sweeps.** Moot here: the head's check-runs are the verdicts.
- **Deviation: file surface amended to include the 35174 note.** This is the correction this record is owed for; judged in ④. Confirmed.
- **Route A rejected.** The reason given holds in the tree: `ObjectRepository` is exported from both entries, and runtime's `keepActionDoorProvenance` passes repositories through unchanged (`action-execution.ts`, its repository mapper returns the repository as given), so `execute` runs on the engine's repository and sees no runtime layer.
- **Out-of-scope note, `carrier: none`: the header's "two of the apis" and row 1b's enumeration still name two apis.** Not accepted as carrier-less. See S2.
- **`open_questions`: none. `security_findings`: none.** I found no finding the dev should have raised beyond S1 and S2.
- **SQL push-down.** No query, id materialisation or in-app join is added. The change is an instance flag and a branch. No finding.
- Nothing to escalate.

### ④ Design judgment

**Security.** The change enforces a refusal the page already documents; it decides no new boundary. Row 1b on `main` already says an action body's system context is refused these writes and that `ObjectRepository.execute` sets the mark; this path was a stated miss of that rule, and the module header says outright that neither flag is a security boundary (a host handler holds the engine, whose `createContext({ isSystem: true })` builds an unmarked system api). No reach is added or removed for host code.

Paths that must stay allowed, each read in the code:
- *The audit writer.* The only production caller of `platformSystemApi` is `plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts:1526`, on a hook's api. A hook's api is `buildHookApi(opCtx.context)` at all five dispatch sites (`engine-insert.ts:656`, `engine-update.ts:703`, `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts:251`, `engine-find.ts:565` and `:883`), and `buildHookApi` is `new ScopedContext(...)` over the write's context, never `derive` from the writer's api. So a hook fired by a dispatched handler's write holds an unflagged api and the mark still comes off. The test's first CONTROL pins this.
- *A host handler's permanent delete.* The flag is separate from `appAuthored`; `ScopedContextFacet.object` wraps the repository only on `appAuthored`, which `execute` never sets. The second CONTROL pins it, on the api and on `platformSystemApi` of it.
- *Every other system context.* `createContext` (`engine-compatibility-section.ts:127`), `buildHookApi` and `appAuthoredHookApi` construct without flagging; only `execute` and a flagged parent's `derive` add to the set.

Flag leak: the set grows only at those two sites, and `derive` is the single constructor behind `sudo()`, `withRunAs(...)`, both transaction branches, `[PLATFORM_SYSTEM_API]` and the seeds. It cannot reach an api not descended from a dispatched action's. Entries are weakly held.

Attempts to break it:
- `sudo()`, then `platformSystemApi`: `derive` flags the child; pinned (`sudo` route).
- Transaction: the joined and owned branches go through `derive`; the no-transaction-support branch hands back `this.facade`, the flagged instance itself. Pinned for the owned branch (`trx` route).
- `withRunAs('user')`, then `platformSystemApi`: child flagged, the spread keeps the mark, `sudo()` re-elevates with it. `withRunAs` with no `userId` returns `UnscopedHookApi`, which has no such member, so `platformSystemApi` answers `undefined`.
- Seeds: `derive` or `this.facade`. Flag kept either way.
- Nested `execute` (the dispatched handler dispatches a third): a fresh api, flagged at construction.
- `execute` from a non-dispatched api (bare engine api, an app-authored hook's wrapped repository, the action door's passed-through repository): all reach the same facet body. Pinned for two of them.
- Chain `platformSystemApi(platformSystemApi(api))`: flagged in, flagged out.
- A handler building its own api from the engine it holds: unflagged, as before, and declared not a boundary.
None broke it.

**`.changeset/35174-action-api-platform-system-api-mark.md` (the correction).**
- The dropped bullet, "Not covered: the api `ctx.api.object(o).execute(name)` hands the action it dispatches is built by the engine, not the action door, so `platformSystemApi` still takes the mark off there": its first half is still true, its conclusion is false at this head (`engine-scoped-context.ts:136`). Shipped beside the 35434 note in one release it would contradict it. Dropping it is correct.
- Every remaining sentence was read against the head. The action-door flag, the permanent delete, the audit writer's api and the derivation walk are runtime's and untouched by this diff. The last bullet ("`@objectstack/objectql` is unchanged but for its module header") describes PR #35383's own change and stays true of it. Nothing else in the note is false, and nothing else in it changed: the diff is that one line.
- **The correction is confirmed.**

**`.changeset/35434-execute-dispatched-action-keeps-mark.md`.**
- Lead paragraph: holds (`execute` marks `'action'`; at the merge base the api was a bare `new ScopedContext`, neither flag).
- Bullet 1: holds, sentence by sentence, per the derive analysis above; `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403 "whichever api dispatched" and the owner stamp are pinned.
- Bullets 2 and 3: hold (the two CONTROLs).
- Bullet 4, second sentence ("No new export, and no published signature changes"): holds (①).
- Bullet 4, first sentence: see S1.

**`packages/objectql/src/engine-object-repository.ts`.** The docblock on the set agrees with the code line by line. `execute` flags the one api it builds.

**`packages/objectql/src/engine-scoped-context.ts`.** `derive` and `platformSystemApi` agree with their docblocks and with `platform-system-api.ts`'s contract. `ScopedContextFacet.sudo.call(this)` on a flagged, non-app-authored api adds no `'hook'` mark and keeps the `'action'` one, which is what the owner stamp needs.

**`packages/objectql/src/platform-system-api.ts`, `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 1b.** The removed clauses were false at this head. Every remaining sentence is true. See S2 for what they now leave out.

Findings:

S1 (should-fix) — `.changeset/35434-execute-dispatched-action-keeps-mark.md`, last bullet: "This closes the path the previous note on `platformSystemApi` named as not covered." At this head no note names it: the same PR deletes that bullet from the 35174 note, and both notes ship in one release. The sentence was written before the fix round and now points at text that will never be published. Reword it to stand alone, for example "This is the path the action-door fix in this release did not reach." Not a must-fix: the note's claims about behaviour are all true.

S2 (should-fix) — `packages/objectql/src/platform-system-api.ts` header ("That line holds on two of the apis the automation is handed") and row 1b ("On an app-authored hook's api and on the api an action door hands its handler ... and on every api derived from either") still enumerate two apis. At this head the line holds on three, and "two of" now reads as a limit the code no longer has. Neither sentence is false, and the card's Done-when asked only for the clause to go, so this does not block; but the page is the census of system-context behaviour and the third api is documented only at the flag. The dev's `carrier: none` is not accepted: name the dispatched action's api in both enumerations, here or on a filed follow-up card.

N1 (nit) — the integration test pins the direct, `sudo()` and owned-transaction routes from two dispatch origins. The `withRunAs(...)` and seed derivations the note also names, a nested `execute`, and the owner stamp from the bare engine origin rest on the single `derive` seam, read in code, not on a case.

No must-fix.
